comments.note: interactive.ts uses a simple while-loop + waitForKeypress() Promise helper pattern, which is easier to test than a one-time Promise callback. The finally block guarantees SIGINT cleanup even if a command throws.

AC1 (Known hotkey): keymap built at entry with insertion-order, first-occurrence-wins deduplication. Command dispatched via keymap.get(ch). Three tests verify dispatch, restoreTerminal-before-run, and long-running vs blocking distinction.
AC2 (Unknown key re-renders): unknown key falls through else block without action; while loop continues and re-enters enterRawMode + renderMenu. Two tests verify re-render count.
AC3 (q exits): running = false triggered by q check before keymap lookup; finally block calls restoreTerminal. Two tests verify exit and cleanup.
AC4 (h triggers help): restoreTerminal + printHelp + waitForKey sequence in h branch. Three tests verify help call, waitForKey, and restoreTerminal order.

AC5 (SIGINT lifecycle): process.on('SIGINT', handler) registered before while loop; process.off in finally block guarantees unregistration on all exit paths. Three tests verify registration, deregistration, and handler behaviour (restoreTerminal + process.kill re-raise).

AC6 (Long-running vs blocking): instanceof Promise discriminant correctly separates the two paths. Three tests cover void path (waitForKey called), async path (waitForKey NOT called), and async path with deferred resolution (awaits correctly).

comments.note: q and h are checked before the keymap lookup, so they always take priority over any command registered with the same key. This is correct UX behaviour but is not documented in comments or jsdoc. Low risk since q/h are reserved by convention.

cmd.run([]) is called without a try/catch. A thrown exception skips the waitForKey call and propagates out of the while loop. The finally block still runs (restoreTerminal + SIGINT cleanup), so terminal state is always restored. Not a blocking issue.

No test for an empty commands array. With no commands, keymap is empty; any key other than q/h triggers a re-render silently. This is correct and safe, but explicit test coverage would strengthen confidence.

comments.note: Medium · A04 Insecure Design · src/menu/interactive.ts lines 59–62. sigintHandler calls process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT') without first unregistering itself via process.off('SIGINT', sigintHandler). Because process.on() registers a persistent listener, the re-raised SIGINT is delivered back to the same handler. The finally block that calls process.off() never executes: waitForKeypress() is awaiting a keypress event whose listener was already removed by restoreTerminal(), leaving the Promise permanently orphaned. The net effect is repeated SIGINT re-deliveries in a tight event-loop cycle — the process spins rather than exiting cleanly on Ctrl+C. Remediation: add process.off('SIGINT', sigintHandler) as the first line of sigintHandler before restoreTerminal() and process.kill().

FAIL — one Blocking issue: SIGINT handler event-loop spin. The sigintHandler calls restoreTerminal() then process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT') without first unregistering itself via process.off('SIGINT', sigintHandler). restoreTerminal() orphans the waitForKeypress() Promise (removes its stdin listener), so the finally block never executes. The re-raised SIGINT is immediately redelivered to the same handler, producing an infinite event-loop spin on every Ctrl+C.
All other dimensions are clean: hotkey dispatch, q/h handling, long-running vs blocking distinction, barrel export, and test coverage are all solid.
Remediation: add process.off('SIGINT', sigintHandler) as the FIRST statement of sigintHandler. Add a regression test verifying the self-unregistration (not just the process.kill call).

comments.note:
BLOCKING: SIGINT handler spin loop in src/menu/interactive.ts lines 56-59.

The handler (1) calls restoreTerminal() — which removes the stdin keypress listener, permanently orphaning the waitForKeypress() Promise — then (2) calls process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT') without first unregistering itself. Because a persistent listener is still registered, the re-raised SIGINT is delivered back to the same sigintHandler on the very next event-loop tick. The finally block (which calls process.off()) cannot execute because the awaited Promise is permanently orphaned. Result: process.kill + restoreTerminal spin indefinitely on every Ctrl+C press.

Remediation (one line): add `process.off('SIGINT', sigintHandler)` as the FIRST statement in sigintHandler, before restoreTerminal() and process.kill(). This ensures the re-raised SIGINT reaches the default Node.js exit handler, not the registered listener.

Additionally, add a regression test that verifies process.off('SIGINT', sigintHandler) was called DURING the sigintHandler invocation (not just in the finally block). The current SIGINT test only checks that process.kill was called, which does not cover the self-unregistration.
